newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican 1996 avocado exports to rise 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexican 1996 avocado exports to rise 10 percent.

text.p: Mexican avocado exports should reach 30,000 tonnes in 1996, up 10 percent from last year, according to a spokesman for Mexico's Avocado Exporters' Association.
"We have 10 percent more than last year in terms of 1996 exports ... about 30,000 or 31,000 tonnes," association director Ricardo Salgado told Reuters.

The association, which represents 80 percent of Mexican exporters, said its members had sold 1,000 tonnes of avocados each week for the past three weeks. November's exports were 15 percent higher than last month, he said.
More than 80 percent of exports are sold to Europe, 10 percent to Canada, eight percent to Japan and the remainder to Central America, the association said.
"Production has been a little low," Salgado said, estimating about 700,000 tonnes would be produced by the end of the year from about one million tonnes in 1995.
Salgado said the association expects the U.S. government to abolish its 80-year ban on Mexican avocado exports by the end of the year.
